messages:
zoe: hey team — urgent: my partner had to see ER while we're traveling and the hospital is refusing to accept the digital e-card because the last name on the insurer portal is my maiden name (we recently updated benefits but the portal shows old name). They say the name on the claim must match the ID on file or they'll deny. Can people ops issue anything temporary to avoid out-of-pocket?

sara (People Ops): hi zoe  sorry to hear. Short answer: yes, we can provide a rapid proof-of-coverage letter and confirmation of dependent enrollment. Also you should get the insurer to confirm coverage by phone and get a reference number. Two quick paths: 1) we send a coverage verification letter you can show at billing, 2) insurer issues a provider verification that the member is covered despite name mismatch.

zoe: how fast? hospital wants something now.

sara (People Ops): we can produce a People Ops coverage letter in < 2 hours. It will state member name, DOB, member ID, group number, effective date, and note that legal name update is in process. Use this copy at registration and ask hospital to accept it with an ID + screenshot of e-card. Also call insurer provider line to get confirmation and note the rep name and case number.

benefits-bot: automated note  For inpatient/ER services, hospitals will often accept a coverage letter plus e-card. If the hospital still insists, request that billing mark the claim as "coverage verified - name discrepancy" and attach the provider phone confirmation to the claim to avoid auto-denial.

claims-rep: insurer tip: when you call provider services, give them member ID, DOB, and claim service date. Ask them to annotate the member record with the legal name change note and to provide a verbal confirmation so the hospital can include the rep name and reference number on the claim. That speeds up adjudication.

zoe: can you paste the coverage letter template? i'll show to intake.

sara (People Ops): yep — copy/paste this into email or print: 

```
[Redwood Inference People Ops Letterhead]

Date: [MM/DD/YYYY]

To whom it may concern,

This letter confirms that [Member Full Name (current legal name)] (DOB: [MM/DD/YYYY], Member ID: [########]) is enrolled in Redwood Inference's group health plan (Plan: Redwood Choice PPO, Group #: [######]) with an active coverage effective date of [MM/DD/YYYY]. A legal name update for this member is currently being processed and the insurer portal may display a prior surname. Please accept this letter along with a photo of the member's government ID and the digital insurance e-card as proof of coverage for medical services provided on [service date].

If you require verification from the insurer, please contact [Insurer Provider Line] and reference Member ID [########] and date of service [MM/DD/YYYY]. For People Ops assistance, email people-ops@redwood.com.

Sincerely,
[People Ops]
```

zoe: thank you. should I also ask billing to add any special claim modifiers?

claims-rep: yes ask them to note on the claim: "V67.49 - Name change" or add the insurer's specifier "Name discrepancy - provider verified" in the claim remarks. If they include the insurer rep name and reference number in the claim notes, it helps prevent automatic denial.

sara (People Ops): zoe  DM me a photo of the e-card and the gov ID and I will generate the PDF letter and call the insurer provider line to get a verification number. Keep screenshots of any phone confirmations. If a denial happens later, forward the EOB to people-ops@redwood.com and we'll escalate to insurer appeals. Good luck — please keep us updated. :heart:
